title: Clone risk action gated only on `risk.read` — no `risk.write`/`risk.create` check; no classification warning for Restricted/Confidential risks
description: Clone risk action button only checks `risk.read` permission. No `risk.write` or `risk.create` guard. No warning when cloning a `Restricted` or `Confidential` risk that the clone will inherit the same classification.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: clone action in risks/page.jsx is wrapped in `<PermissionHide permission="risk.create" allowProjectGrant>`, and a classification-inherited warning (`cloneClassificationWarning`) is shown in the clone confirmation modal before cloning. Confirmed fixed.

title: `getRiskColor` maps score < 5 and score 5–9 to identical green — no "Very Low" zone; negligible risks indistinguishable from Low
description: `getRiskColor` maps both `score < 5` and `score 5–9` to green. There is no "Very Low" zone. Negligible risks (score 1–4) are visually identical to Low risks (score 5–9).
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: RiskHeatMap.jsx:75-80 now defines 5 distinct zones (Critical>=20 red, High>=15 orange, Medium>=9 yellow, Low>=4 green, Very Low<4 teal) with distinct colors. Confirmed fixed.

title: `reviewCadence = Math.max(0, 100 − reviewDue × 10)` penalises large organisations disproportionately — flat 0% for ≥ 10 overdue reviews
description: `reviewCadence = Math.max(0, 100 − reviewDue × 10)` — any organisation with 10+ overdue reviews scores 0% regardless of total risk count. A 500-risk org with 10 overdue is penalised identically to a 20-risk org with 10 overdue.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: governance/page.jsx:158-160 now computes `reviewCadence = Math.max(0, Math.round((1 - overdueReviews/totalRisks) * 100))` — proportional to total risk count, not a flat per-overdue-review penalty. Confirmed fixed.

title: Prediction factor strings not linked to source data — `riskId` exists but no UI link; auditor cannot verify basis for AI-generated predictions
description: Prediction factor strings contain a `riskId` reference but no clickable UI link. Auditors cannot navigate from a prediction to the underlying risk record that generated it.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: ai-predictions/page.jsx:598-606 now derives `factorRiskId` from `factor.riskId || factor.sourceRiskId` and renders `href={'/risk-center/risks/' + factorRiskId}` when present. Confirmed fixed.

title: No year-over-year comparison — single time-window only; auditor cannot demonstrate continual improvement per ISO cl. 10.1
description: Trends page supports only a single time-window selection. No option to overlay a prior period or compare current year vs. prior year risk counts/scores.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: trends/page.jsx's `timeRange` selector still offers only 30d/90d/180d/1y as a single window (lines 389-399) — no comparison/overlay/prior-period option exists anywhere in the file (grepped for previousYear/comparisonData/vsLastYear/priorYear/YoY — zero matches). Not fixed; re-opened.
firstDetected: 2026-08-27 (re-opened; originally logged against the pre-restructure file)

title: No staleness indicator on triage items — queue may contain findings from a 6-week-old Prowler scan that are already remediated
description: Triage queue items from Prowler, VendorService, etc. show no `lastScanAt` or age indicator. A finding from a 6-week-old Prowler scan that has since been remediated appears identical to a fresh finding.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: ModuleRiskTriageQueue.jsx:131-136 defines `getStaleness(createdAt)` with aging(14d)/stale(30d)/very-stale(42d) thresholds plus staleness filter options. Confirmed fixed.

title: AI-returned `likelihood` and `impact` stored as-is without bounds clamping — out-of-range values (0 or 6) produce invalid score (0 or 30)
description: AI-returned `likelihood` and `impact` values stored as-is. Out-of-range values (0 or 6+) produce invalid scores (0 or 30+) that fall outside the 5×5 heat map grid, causing rendering errors or misplacement.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: AIRiskDraftModal.jsx:188-192 clamps via `Math.max(1, Math.min(5, Math.round(Number(draft.likelihood ?? 3))))` (same for impact) and shows a warning when clamping occurred. Confirmed fixed.

title: No self-acceptance prevention — risk owner can select themselves as approver; four-eyes principle not enforced
description: The approver dropdown is not filtered to exclude the risk owner or creator. Risk owners can select themselves as the approver for their own risk acceptance.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: RiskAcceptanceWorkflow.jsx:706-712 filters `eligibleApprovers` to exclude `currentUser._id`/`.id`, `risk.ownerId`, and `risk.createdBy`. Confirmed fixed (though the workflow is unreachable in practice for real backend data per new record RR-048).

title: Treatment description has no minimum length — trivial entries (`TBD`, `see ticket`) accepted as documented treatment evidence
description: Treatment description input has no minimum length validation. Entries like `TBD` or `see ticket` are accepted as documented treatment evidence.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: RiskTreatmentPanel.jsx:408-508 enforces a visible 30-char minimum with a disabled-save state below that threshold. Confirmed fixed.

title: `submitAcceptanceRequest` stores `email: ''` and `name: ''` for all approvers — acceptance audit trail contains no human-readable approver identity beyond `ObjectId`
description: In `submitAcceptanceRequest`, approvers are constructed as `data.approverIds.map((id) => ({ userId: new ObjectId(id), email: '', name: '' }))`. No user lookup is performed to populate `email` and `name`. All acceptance records in the database store blank string identity for every approver — only `userId` (ObjectId) is preserved.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: risk.repository.ts:1502-1513 now performs a real `usersCollection.find({_id: {$in: ...}})` lookup and populates `email`/`name` from the matched user documents. Confirmed fixed.

title: `AcceptanceRequestSchema` enforces `justification: z.string().min(1)` — server-side accepts single-char justification; 50-char advisory is frontend-only
description: `AcceptanceRequestSchema` defines `justification: z.string().min(1).max(2000)`. The frontend shows an advisory hint of 50 characters minimum, but the backend schema accepts any non-empty string. A one-character justification (`x`) passes Zod validation and is persisted as a documented risk acceptance rationale. `RenewalRequestSchema` has the same gap: `justification: z.string().min(1).max(2000)`.
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: validation.ts:443 and :457 both now enforce `justification: z.string().min(50, 'Justification must be at least 50 characters...').max(2000)` server-side. Confirmed fixed.

title: `getTrends` `$group` stage groups by month only, not month+year — data from different years collapses into the same bucket
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: the trends aggregation was relocated from risk.repository.ts to RiskCenterService.ts's `getTrendsData`, which now groups via `$dateToString: {format: '%Y-%m-%d', date: '$createdAt'}` — full date (year+month+day), not month-only. Confirmed fixed (and superseded — even finer-grained than the original fix would have required).

title: `riskReduction` NaN when inherentRiskScore = 0 — already guarded with `inherentRiskScore > 0 ? ... : 0` at line ~840
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: `const riskReduction = inherentRiskScore > 0 ? Math.round(...) : 0;` confirmed present (now at line 823-825). Still a genuine false positive.

title: `new Date(acceptance?.expiryDate).toLocaleDateString()` passes null/undefined to `Date()` — displays 'Invalid Date' instead of a guarded fallback
affectedFiles: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/risk-register/RiskAcceptanceWorkflow.jsx:889 (UNGUARDED — `new Date(acceptance.expiryDate).toLocaleDateString()` inside the approved/renewed block, no ternary/fallback)
vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/risk-register/RiskAcceptanceWorkflow.jsx:942 (UNGUARDED — `new Date(acceptance.rejectedAt).toLocaleDateString()` inside the rejected block, no fallback)
description: The specific pattern originally cited was fixed at at least 3 locations (lines 292, 379, 393) with a proper `acceptance?.expiryDate ? new Date(...).toLocaleDateString() : 'No expiry set'` ternary. However, re-verification found the same class of defect still present, unguarded, at two other renders in the same file: line 889 (Valid Until display in the approved/renewed summary block) and line 942 (rejection date in the rejected block). Given the real backend field is `acceptance.validUntil`, not `acceptance.expiryDate` (see RR-048), `acceptance.expiryDate` is undefined for any risk sourced from the real API, so line 889 renders 'Invalid Date' in production on every approved/renewed acceptance view.

title: Expiry notifier uses stale risk title snapshot — notifier fetches directly from `risksCollection` (live data), not a snapshot
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-27: `const riskName: string = risk.name || risk.title || riskId;` (line 306) derives from the live `this.risksCollection.find(...)` result fetched fresh each run, not a cached/stale snapshot. Confirmed still a genuine false positive.

component: Accepted Risks Page — API Call Shape
title: `getAcceptedRisks` omits `projectId` from the query when no project is selected, but the backend route requires it — production requests 400 and silently fall back to an empty list with no error shown
description: `riskService.getAcceptedRisks` only includes `projectId` in the querystring when it is truthy (`...(projectId && { projectId })`), and the accepted-risks page calls it with `selectedProject?._id`, which is `undefined` whenever no project is selected. The backend route's querystring schema marks `projectId` as `required`, and the handler explicitly returns `400 { error: 'projectId is required and must be a valid ObjectId' }` when it is missing. In `fetchAcceptedRisks`, this 400 is caught, logged via `console.warn`, and — outside `NODE_ENV === 'development'` — the page simply falls back to an empty `acceptedRisks` array with no user-facing error, so the page silently shows 'No Accepted Risks Found' instead of surfacing that a project needs to be selected. This is a narrower instance of the same 'optional-projectId call shape vs required-projectId backend route' pattern this platform has hit before in other modules.

title: Risk Center's own main dashboard (page.jsx) has no heat map visualization at all — RiskHeatMap.jsx is fully built and correctly fixed (RR-013/RR-021) but is only wired into the SCRC and vCISO Executive Dashboard pages, not into risk-center's own home page
description: This module's own architecture notes and Area 7 QA coverage describe 'page.jsx — main dashboard (heat map, KPIs, governance radar, trending stats)' as a current Risk Center feature. Direct inspection of `(private)/risk-center/page.jsx` found zero references to 'heat', 'Heat', or 'Matrix' anywhere in the 1523-line file, and `RiskHeatMap` is not imported. The component itself is a well-built, actively-maintained 634-line component with the RR-013/RR-021 fixes genuinely present — but its only two real call sites in the entire repo are `SCRCDashboard.jsx` and the vCISO `executive-dashboard/page.jsx`, both outside the risk-center module. Users visiting the Risk Center dashboard itself see no 5x5 heat map / risk matrix visualization, despite it being a core ISO 31000 §6.4 risk-visualization expectation for a risk register/center product.

title: `NotificationService.notifyApprovalRequest` is fully implemented but has zero callers anywhere in the service — no risk-acceptance/approval action ever notifies an approver, consistent with the already-known broken acceptance workflow (RR-046/047/048)
description:
**Checklist row:** §5.1 — Key lifecycle events dispatch a notification: assignment, due-date approaching/overdue, approval requested, approval decision, status change — each fires through the standard dispatch pipeline.
**Files:** `NotificationService.ts` implements a genuinely comprehensive set of dispatch methods — `notifyRiskAssignment` (called on create/reassign, confirmed working in `RiskRegisterService.ts:250,450,462`), `notifyEscalation` (called in `risk-register.routes.ts:1216`), `notifySLABreach`/`notifyAcceptanceExpiry`/`notifyTreatmentOverdue` (all called from the scheduled `jobs/alerts.job.ts`) — but `notifyApprovalRequest` (lines 386-433) has zero callers anywhere in `risk-management-service/src/`, confirmed by a repo-wide grep matching only its own definition.
**Root Cause:** This lines up exactly with the already-logged `RR-046`/`RR-047`/`RR-048` findings — the risk-acceptance workflow's actual submission/approval code path (`AcceptanceRequestForm`/`ApprovalDecisionForm` and their backend handlers) is confirmed broken (a `projectId` ReferenceError, `approvers` hardcoded to `[]`, a frontend/backend status-vocabulary mismatch) — so the one call site that should invoke `notifyApprovalRequest` (when a risk-acceptance request is actually submitted to a real approver) was either never written or never reached, leaving the notification method itself an orphaned, untested stub.
**Impact:** Independent of RR-046/047/048's functional bugs, this is a checklist-specific gap worth tracking on its own: even once the acceptance workflow's submission path is fixed, nothing currently calls `notifyApprovalRequest` to alert the assigned approver that a decision is waiting on them — the fix for RR-047 (populating `approvers`) does not, by itself, guarantee this notification gets wired in.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
When fixing `RR-047` (populating `approvers` in `AcceptanceRequestForm`/`ApprovalDecisionForm`'s backend handler), add a call to `notificationService.notifyApprovalRequest(...)` for each approver once the acceptance request is actually created/submitted — mirroring the same `notifyRiskAssignment` call-site pattern already working in `RiskRegisterService.ts:250`. Add a regression test asserting `notifyApprovalRequest` is called with the correct approver list when a risk-acceptance request is submitted.
